DIRECTV Insider 2026 head coaching change summary (2026-08-26)

ARI.brief: Mike LaFleur takes over as head coach after running a Rams offense that led the NFL in yards and points, and he inherits a transitional roster. Jacoby Brissett is the Week 1 starter with Gardner Minshew and rookie third-rounder Carson Beck behind him, so the passing game has a competent but low-ceiling trigger. Arizona spent the No. 3 overall pick on RB Jeremiyah Love and the backfield is thin behind him: James Conner (foot) and Trey Benson (knee) both opened on IR. The defense ranked 29th in points allowed last year and was not meaningfully upgraded, which should keep Arizona playing from behind and throwing.

ATL.brief: Kevin Stefanski replaces Raheem Morris and named Tua Tagovailoa the Week 1 starter, Atlanta's sixth different opening-day quarterback in six years. Michael Penix Jr. is out after a third ACL tear in five years, so there is no short-term quarterback competition. The skill group is strong - Bijan Robinson, Drake London and a Kyle Pitts coming off a second-team All-Pro season - and Stefanski's play-action, condensed-formation scheme historically supports tight ends and a heavy lead back. Warm-weather NFC South games and a Robinson-centered run game should keep Tagovailoa's floor stable even if the ceiling is capped.

BAL.brief: Jesse Minter is the first new Ravens head coach in nearly 20 years, taking over a team that missed the playoffs for only the second time in eight years. Lamar Jackson remains the engine and Derrick Henry is still handling the goal-line work despite entering his age-32 season. The offensive staff turned over completely with Todd Monken leaving for Cleveland, which is the main unknown for Mark Andrews and Rashod Bateman. Baltimore signed Trey Hendrickson and drafted edge Zion Young, so game scripts should be more favorable than last season.

BUF.brief: Joe Brady was promoted from offensive coordinator to head coach, so continuity for Josh Allen is the point of the hire. Buffalo led the NFL in rushing last year behind James Cook III and Allen, and added DJ Moore from Chicago to a receiving corps that badly needed a primary target. The fundamental flaw is unaddressed: the Bills were 28th in rushing yards allowed and near last in rushing touchdowns allowed, which means shootouts and pass volume in bad matchups. Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman are both dealing with injuries entering Week 1.

CAR.brief: Carolina returns Bryce Young for a fourth season with Tetairoa McMillan, the reigning Offensive Rookie of the Year, as the clear No. 1 target. The backfield lost Rico Dowdle to Pittsburgh and is now a Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) and Jonathon Brooks question mark, with Brooks having missed all of 2025 after retearing an ACL. Darren Waller is the starting tight end. The offense has not been efficient enough to support more than one or two reliable weekly starters.

CHI.brief: Ben Johnson's second year in Chicago has Caleb Williams coming off a real leap - top 11 among quarterbacks in essentially every volume and rushing category. DJ Moore was traded to Buffalo, which concentrates targets on Rome Odunze, second-year slot Luther Burden III and tight end Colston Loveland, who closed 2025 with four straight double-digit target games. The backfield is a genuine committee between D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai, both listed questionable in Week 1. Pace and red-zone efficiency are the reasons to buy Bears skill players.

CIN.brief: A healthy Joe Burrow is the single biggest swing factor here after injuries limited him to eight games in 2025. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins remain one of the best receiver duos in football, though both are carrying Week 1 injury designations. Chase Brown was a different player once the quarterback play stabilized, averaging 21.2 fantasy points over his final 10 games. The defense lost Trey Hendrickson to Baltimore and remains the reason Cincinnati games stay high-scoring.

CLE.brief: Todd Monken takes over a team openly building for 2027. Deshaun Watson is the Week 1 starter largely because of his cap hit, with Shedeur Sanders behind him and Dillon Gabriel on IR. Cleveland traded Myles Garrett and spent premium picks on offense: KC Concepcion in the first round and Denzel Boston in the second, joining Jerry Jeudy. Quinshon Judkins handled 71% of the designed rush attempts when healthy last year and Harold Fannin Jr. is a legitimate top-five fantasy tight end. Expect negative game scripts and a lot of passing volume from behind.

DAL.brief: Brian Schottenheimer's second year returns essentially the same high-volume passing offense - Dak Prescott led the NFL in completions and played all 17 games. CeeDee Lamb and franchise-tagged George Pickens are both featured, with Jake Ferguson a heavy target share tight end whose production dips when both receivers are healthy. Javonte Williams is coming off a career year with 13 touchdowns. The one real concern is the line: three-time Pro Bowl LG Tyler Smith needs thumb surgery and will miss four to six weeks, with T.J. Bass stepping in.

DEN.brief: Denver is Bo Nix's third year and the receiver room was rebuilt around a Jaylen Waddle trade, joining Courtland Sutton. Nix has finished seventh among quarterbacks in fantasy points in both his seasons on the strength of rushing, not efficiency. The backfield is an unresolved J.K. Dobbins versus RJ Harvey split that neither back has won outright, with rookie Jonah Coleman added in the fourth round. The defense should keep games close and the offense manageable rather than explosive.

DET.brief: Detroit returns Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown intact, with Jameson Williams coming off back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons. David Montgomery was traded to Houston, which removes the primary competition for Gibbs's goal-line work - Gibbs has never finished a season higher than seventh in touches and that should change. Sam LaPorta is questionable with a hip issue and Isiah Pacheco, signed in the offseason, is already on IR with a back injury. The Lions open at home as heavy favorites over New Orleans.

GB.brief: Green Bay's backfield changed completely when Josh Jacobs was placed on the commissioner's exempt list on August 31 over pending misdemeanor charges; he cannot practice or attend games and has no timetable. MarShawn Lloyd is now the listed RB1 with Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson behind him. Jordan Love has been an efficient passer without fantasy volume the past two years, throwing to Christian Watson, Jayden Reed and second-year Matthew Golden. Tucker Kraft is back from a Week 9 ACL tear and carries a Week 1 questionable tag. Dontayvion Wicks was traded to Philadelphia.

HOU.brief: Houston traded for David Montgomery and Kayshon Boutte and moved on from little else, so the offense still runs through Nico Collins with C.J. Stroud under center. Stroud's passing production has declined in each of his three seasons, which is the core problem for everyone in this passing game. Tank Dell opened on IR with a knee injury and rookie Jaylin Noel is questionable with a hamstring. The defense is the strength and is ranked first or second among fantasy units in most places.

IND.brief: Daniel Jones re-signed and holds the job, with Anthony Richardson officially named the backup. Jonathan Taylor is coming off an NFL-leading carry and touchdown season and is the offense's identity. Tyler Warren was substantially better with a healthy Jones (13.1 fantasy points per game versus 6.3 without) and is questionable with a groin injury. Alec Pierce was paid like a No. 1 receiver in the offseason, and Keenan Allen was added at 34 as a possession complement to Pierce and slot man Josh Downs.

JAX.brief: Liam Coen's second year returns Trevor Lawrence coming off a breakout in volume terms - top seven in attempts, completions, yards and touchdowns. Travis Etienne Jr. left for New Orleans, handing the backfield to second-year Bhayshul Tuten with Chris Rodriguez Jr. and LeQuint Allen Jr. behind him. Brian Thomas Jr. and Jakobi Meyers headline a deep receiver group, and Parker Washington is listed as the starting slot after a strong finish to 2025. Travis Hunter is now a full-time defender, which is the key detail on his fantasy profile.

KC.brief: Patrick Mahomes is on track to start Week 1 against Denver, roughly nine months after December surgery on a torn ACL and LCL. He has not missed practice since being cleared in July, but he is carrying a questionable designation and his efficiency had already dipped in each of the last three seasons. Kansas City signed Kenneth Walker III, the reigning Super Bowl MVP, to be the feature back in an Andy Reid offense. Rashee Rice is finally healthy and unsuspended, with Xavier Worthy and a 36-year-old Travis Kelce alongside him.

LV.brief: Klint Kubiak arrives from Seattle, where he turned a Sam Darnold offense into a top-10 unit that won the Super Bowl. Kirk Cousins opens as the starter ahead of No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza, and that timeline is the single biggest variable for every Raiders pass catcher. Brock Bowers is the focal point of the passing game and Ashton Jeanty enters Year 2 in what should be a better offense, though he is questionable with a knee issue. Tre Tucker is the nominal WR1 in a thin receiver room.

LAC.brief: Jim Harbaugh's Chargers return Justin Herbert with Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, and Omarion Hampton is set for a full second-season workload after an injury-shortened but productive rookie year. The tight end room was reshaped: rookie-year breakout Oronde Gadsden II is listed ahead of newly signed David Njoku. Los Angeles lost defensive coordinator Jesse Minter to the Baltimore head job, the one real staff subtraction. Kicker Cameron Dicker is questionable for Week 1.

LAR.brief: The Rams are the offseason's spending story, building a super team around 38-year-old reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, who led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns. Mike LaFleur left to become Arizona's head coach, so the play-calling continuity behind Stafford's career year is gone. Puka Nacua and Davante Adams headline the passing game and Kyren Williams remains the lead back with Blake Corum behind him. Los Angeles overhauled the secondary with a trade for Trent McDuffie and the signing of Jaylen Watson, and opens the season in Melbourne against San Francisco on a Thursday.

MIA.brief: Miami is a full teardown under new head coach Jeff Hafley. Mike McDaniel, Tua Tagovailoa and Jaylen Waddle are all gone, and Malik Willis gets his first extended shot as a starter after two years backing up Jordan Love. De'Von Achane is the only reliable fantasy asset - three straight seasons of 11 or 12 touchdowns and elite receiving usage. The receiver room is now Malik Washington plus rookies Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell, and Greg Dulcich is the starting tight end. Expect low team totals and a heavy Achane target share.

MIN.brief: Kyler Murray signed with Minnesota and beat out J.J. McCarthy for the job, which raises the rushing floor of this offense considerably over last season. Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison return with Jauan Jennings added in May and T.J. Hockenson still trying to recapture his 2023 form. The backfield is a genuine split between 31-year-old Aaron Jones Sr., listed as RB1, and Jordan Mason. Harrison Smith returned on a one-year deal to anchor a defense that is a strong streaming unit.

NE.brief: Mike Vrabel's Patriots won the AFC East and reached the Super Bowl, and they doubled down by trading for A.J. Brown in June to pair with Drake Maye, the MVP runner-up. Maye led the league in completion percentage and yards per attempt and trailed only Josh Allen in fantasy points. The backfield remains a Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson committee that Stevenson has won more often than not, though Henderson is the more efficient back. New England extended Christian Gonzalez on a four-year, $135 million deal to keep the secondary intact.

NO.brief: Kellen Moore's second year in New Orleans has Tyler Shough as the starter after he scored 17-plus fantasy points in seven of nine full games as a rookie. The supporting cast is genuinely better: Travis Etienne Jr. signed to lead the backfield and Chris Olave is coming off a career year with 100 catches. First-round rookie Jordyn Tyson opened on IR with a hamstring strain, which pushes Devaughn Vele into the No. 2 receiver role. Alvin Kamara is now RB4 on the depth chart at 31 and carrying a knee designation.

NYG.brief: John Harbaugh takes his first new job in 20 years and inherits a 4-13 roster with real young talent. Jaxson Dart was an elite rushing quarterback as a rookie - top five at the position in carries, rushing yards and touchdowns inside the 5 - but spent too much time in the medical tent. Malik Nabers has shed the noncontact jersey and returned to team periods after ACL surgery, but the Giants have not guaranteed him for Week 1. Cam Skattebo is healthy and listed as RB1 with Najee Harris behind him, and Harbaugh brought Isaiah Likely over from Baltimore. Darius Slayton was released on September 7.

NYJ.brief: Mike LaFleur takes over play-calling after two Rams offenses that finished top eight in yards and points, including a No. 1 finish last year. Geno Smith was traded in to stabilize the position, which matters most for Garrett Wilson, who has never had a top-20 fantasy season despite consistently elite target volume. Breece Hall was franchise tagged and is questionable with a thigh injury, with Braelon Allen behind him. Rookie first-rounder Omar Cooper Jr. and second-year Adonai Mitchell round out the receiver room, and Mason Taylor played 81% of the snaps at tight end as a rookie.

PHI.brief: Philadelphia returns Jalen Hurts, Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert, with A.J. Brown traded to New England. That subtraction is the whole story for Smith, who has spent five seasons as the second option and now moves into the primary role. Hurts's rushing production collapsed last year - 105 carries after four straight seasons of 139 or more - which is what dropped him from a top-five to an eighth-place fantasy quarterback. First-round rookie Makai Lemon and newly acquired Dontayvion Wicks fill out the receiver room. Tank Bigsby is the primary backup behind Barkley.

PIT.brief: Mike McCarthy replaces Mike Tomlin, who stepped down to become an NBC analyst, and reunites with Aaron Rodgers. McCarthy's offenses in Dallas finished top five three straight years, which is the bull case for everyone here. Pittsburgh traded for Michael Pittman Jr. and extended him, signed Rico Dowdle to pair with Jaylen Warren, and drafted receiver Germie Bernard in the second round. Rodgers is 42 and the offense finished in the bottom third last season, so the volume case is stronger than the efficiency case. DK Metcalf and Pittman are both questionable for Week 1.

SEA.brief: The defending Super Bowl champions lost offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak to the Raiders head job, which is the biggest change to an offense that finished top 10. Sam Darnold returns and Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off an Offensive Player of the Year season in which he led all receivers in target share, yards and yards per route run. The backfield was gutted: Kenneth Walker III signed with Kansas City and Zach Charbonnet opened on PUP with an ACL tear, leaving rookie second-rounder Jadarian Price as the listed starter. Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed are the complementary receivers.

SF.brief: San Francisco opens in Melbourne against the Rams on Thursday night with two major bodies still uncertain. George Kittle practiced in full uniform in Australia and is trending toward playing after an Achilles tear in January's wild-card game, and Christian McCaffrey was also fully dressed for a second straight practice. The receiver room was rebuilt around 33-year-old Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel Sr. back for a second stint, and second-round rookie De'Zhaun Stribling. Brock Purdy has quietly finished top 10 in fantasy points per game three years running when healthy.

TB.brief: Tampa Bay returns Baker Mayfield for a fourth season, with Emeka Egbuka now the nominal WR1 and Chris Godwin Jr. back from injuries that limited him to 16 games over two years. Mike Evans left for San Francisco, which frees up 27 end-zone targets' worth of red-zone work from last season for the rest of the room. Bucky Irving needs to bounce back from a 3.40 yards-per-carry season, with Kenny Gainwell signed as the primary complement. Cade Otton remains the tight end in a role that has never produced much target volume.

TEN.brief: Robert Saleh takes over a team that has gone 3-14 in consecutive seasons and made surrounding Cam Ward with weapons the offseason priority - Carnell Tate went fourth overall and Wan'Dale Robinson signed a four-year deal, joining Calvin Ridley. Ward was busy as a rookie, eighth in the league in dropbacks, but managed only 5.9 yards per attempt. Tony Pollard has handled 67% of the designed rush attempts across two seasons without producing more than five touchdowns in either. Chig Okonkwo left for Washington, opening the tight end job for second-year Gunnar Helm.

WAS.brief: Washington enters Week 1 markedly healthier than last season, when Jayden Daniels missed 10 games and Terry McLaurin missed seven. Daniels's rushing is the reason to own him and the reason his injury risk is real. Stefon Diggs signed in August after being released by New England, and third-round rookie Antonio Williams is in the slot. The backfield is a Jacory Croskey-Merritt and Rachaad White split with both listed questionable, and Chig Okonkwo arrives from Tennessee at tight end. Washington opens on the road at Philadelphia.

4984.outlook: Unanimous QB1 across all eight sources, the only player in the file with a perfect 1.0 average. Allen has finished no worse than second among quarterbacks in six straight seasons and remains a top-five rusher at the position every year of his career. Passing volume has actually declined - 14th or lower in attempts each of the last two years - but the rushing floor makes that irrelevant. Joe Brady's promotion from coordinator to head coach means no scheme change, and DJ Moore arrives as the primary outside target Buffalo lacked.
4984.watch: Whether Brady's move upstairs changes the play-calling voice in Allen's ear.

4881.outlook: QB2 consensus with only FantasyPros dynasty and Fantasy Football Calculator dissenting at QB4. Jackson's fantasy value has never depended on volume, and the rushing profile is intact entering his age-29 season. The variable is a completely new coaching staff under first-time head coach Jesse Minter, with the entire Todd Monken offense gone to Cleveland. Derrick Henry continuing to absorb goal-line carries caps the rushing touchdown ceiling somewhat.
4881.watch: How the new coordinator uses Jackson's designed runs in the red zone.

11564.outlook: Coming off a breakout in which he led the NFL in completion percentage (72%) and yards per attempt (8.9) and trailed only Josh Allen in fantasy points, points per game and top-10 weeks. A.J. Brown was traded in specifically to give him a true alpha target. Maye also finished top five among quarterbacks in rush attempts and yards, which is what separates his ceiling from the pocket passers ranked near him. Sources are tight: eight rankings between QB2 and QB5.
11564.watch: Whether the Brown addition raises efficiency or just concentrates targets.

6770.outlook: Burrow has missed at least six games in three of six pro seasons, including two of the last three, and that is the entire risk case. When active in 2025 he was a top-12 weekly scorer in five of his final six games, though a near-total lack of rushing (41 yards on 14 carries) caps his ceiling relative to Allen, Maye and Daniels. A full season with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins healthy gets him back to the top-five range he hit in both of his complete campaigns.
6770.watch: Availability - he has no rushing floor to fall back on.

11566.outlook: Played only seven games last year and was less dominant when active (16.3 points per game versus 20.9 as a rookie), but the rushing profile held up at 58-278-2 in those seven appearances. Washington is meaningfully healthier entering Week 1 and added Stefon Diggs in August. Daniels is the biggest source spread in the top six: ESPN, NBC and FantasyPros dynasty all have him third while Fantasy Football Calculator has him eighth.
11566.watch: His durability given how much of his value is designed runs.

6904.outlook: The tush-push rushing production collapsed in 2025 - 105 carries and 421 yards after four straight seasons of at least 139 carries and 605 yards - dropping him from a perennial top-five fantasy quarterback to eighth. He offset some of it with a career-high 25 passing touchdowns. A.J. Brown is gone, which concentrates targets on DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert but removes the offense's downfield threat.
6904.watch: Whether Philadelphia restores his goal-line carry volume.

11560.outlook: Finished no lower than 11th among quarterbacks in attempts, completions, yards, passing touchdowns, carries, rushing yards, rushing touchdowns and points per game last season, which is a rare combination of floors. Completion percentage remains a real weakness at 58%, but he has thrown only seven interceptions in each of his two seasons. DJ Moore's departure to Buffalo concentrates targets on Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland in Ben Johnson's second year.
11560.watch: Whether the accuracy improves enough to convert his volume into efficiency.

3294.outlook: Played all 17 games, led the NFL in completions and ranked no lower than fourth in dropbacks, attempts, yards and passing touchdowns. His nine top-10 fantasy weeks tied for third at the position. He offers essentially nothing as a rusher now, so the value is pure volume in a Schottenheimer offense that throws a lot. Left guard Tyler Smith needs thumb surgery and will miss four to six weeks, the one real short-term concern.
3294.watch: Pass protection while Tyler Smith is out.

6797.outlook: Set career highs in carries and rushing yards last season, finishing fifth and second among quarterbacks in those categories, which is what got him to a QB10 finish. The problem is consistency - five top-five weeks and nothing else better than 13th. Herbert has finished between 11th and a similar range in most seasons, which is exactly where the consensus has him again. Ladd McConkey bouncing back matters more to his ceiling than anything else.
6797.watch: Whether the added rushing volume is repeatable or was a one-year artifact.

7523.outlook: Ranked no lower than seventh among quarterbacks in attempts, completions, yards and touchdowns and top 10 in carries, rushing yards and rushing touchdowns, closing with seven straight top-10 fantasy outings. Efficiency has never been the selling point; volume has, and he has finished top 10 in both pass and rush attempts in each of his four full seasons. The receiver room is deep with Brian Thomas Jr., Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington.
7523.watch: Whether Liam Coen keeps calling the same high-volume game.

8183.outlook: Injuries limited him to nine games but he scored 17-plus fantasy points in seven of them, including 26-plus in three straight during Weeks 15-17. He has quietly finished top 10 in points per game three years running. The supporting cast is intact enough if George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey are healthy, though the receiver room turned over to Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel Sr. and a rookie. Opens Thursday in Melbourne against a rebuilt Rams secondary.
8183.watch: Kittle's Achilles and McCaffrey's status for the opener.

12508.outlook: Delivered eight top-10 fantasy weeks as a rookie - tied for fifth most - despite playing the bulk of the snaps in only 12 games, and finished top five among quarterbacks in rush attempts, rushing yards, rushing touchdowns and carries inside the 5. ESPN is the outlier at QB8; the rest of the file has him QB11 to QB16. His aggressive style is both the source of the upside and the durability concern, and John Harbaugh's staff may reduce the designed-run volume.
12508.watch: Whether Harbaugh's staff protects him by cutting the rushing usage.

4046.outlook: Mahomes says he is on track to start Week 1 and has not missed a practice since being cleared in July, roughly nine months after December surgery on a torn ACL and LCL. He is still listed questionable. The 2025 season was split: 24.5 points per game over the first eight weeks, 15.0 over his final six before the tear. His efficiency has dipped three straight seasons and the rushing production that propped up 2025 is the most likely thing to disappear coming off a knee reconstruction. FantasyCalc has his redraft value down 425 in 30 days, the steepest drop of any top-15 quarterback.
4046.watch: Whether the scrambling returns - without it he is a low-ceiling pocket passer.

11563.outlook: Has finished exactly seventh among quarterbacks in fantasy points in both of his seasons, entirely on the strength of rushing rather than passing efficiency (career 6.5 yards per attempt). Last year gave a solid floor - 11 games of 15-plus points - and almost no ceiling. Jaylen Waddle arrives from Miami to pair with Courtland Sutton, which is the first genuine talent upgrade of his career.
11563.watch: Whether Waddle raises his yards per attempt out of the bottom tier.

3163.outlook: Three straight seasons of 4,500-plus yards and 30-plus touchdowns, but his per-game finishes (15th, seventh, 12th) are less impressive than his season totals because he never misses time and never runs. Goff has never cleared 108 rushing yards in a season, which sets a hard ceiling in a format where the top of the position is dual-threat. The Detroit supporting cast is fully intact and the offense should be among the league's best again.
3163.watch: Nothing situational - his ceiling is structural.

421.outlook: Reigning MVP at 38 after leading the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns with nine top-10 fantasy weeks. The regression case is straightforward: no rushing whatsoever (65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons) and a third-place points-per-game finish that was his first top 10 since 2019. Mike LaFleur, the coordinator behind the career year, left to be Arizona's head coach. This is the largest source disagreement at the position - Fantasy Football Calculator has him QB6 while FantasyPros dynasty has him QB27, and the age gap explains most of it.
421.watch: Whether the offense holds up without LaFleur calling plays.

5849.outlook: Signed with Minnesota and beat out J.J. McCarthy for the job. The 2025 season was a five-game disaster where he never cleared 18.3 fantasy points, but prior to that he had finished each of his first six seasons as a top-12 quarterback on a per-game basis. He remains an accurate but conservative passer whose value comes from his legs - 78-572-5 across 17 games in 2024. Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison are a clear upgrade on what he had in Arizona.
5849.watch: Whether the rushing volume returns after an injury-shortened year.

6804.outlook: One of the league's best passers by QBR - ninth, fifth and third in his three years starting - with almost none of it converting to fantasy production. He has finished 17th and 21st the past two seasons on the back of low pass volume (19th in attempts both years) and almost no rushing (282 yards and one touchdown across two seasons combined). NBC is the outlier at QB12; everyone else has him QB15 or worse. Josh Jacobs's absence could push more offense through the air.
6804.watch: Whether Green Bay's pass volume rises with Jacobs unavailable.

4892.outlook: Three straight top-12 fantasy campaigns but 2025 was a clear step back - 26 touchdowns after 41 in 2024, and only four top-10 weekly finishes. He was not fully healthy for much of it and still finished top 10 in key volume categories. Mike Evans leaving for San Francisco removes his most reliable red-zone target and 27 end-zone looks from the offense.
4892.watch: Whether Emeka Egbuka can absorb Evans's red-zone role.

12545.outlook: One of the genuine second-half surprises of 2025, scoring 17-plus fantasy points in seven of his nine full games including six straight to close. He produced with both his arm (250.1 yards per game) and legs (19.3 rushing yards per game, three touchdowns) but never topped 22 fantasy points in a game. Travis Etienne Jr. and a healthy Chris Olave should raise the floor. Jordyn Tyson opening on IR removes the rookie target he was expected to grow with.
12545.watch: Whether the supporting-cast upgrade produces a real ceiling.

8161.outlook: Gets his first extended starting job after two years backing up Jordan Love, with only 155 career pass attempts to evaluate. He was efficient in limited work but the Miami supporting cast is the worst in the league after the teardown - Malik Washington and two third-round rookies at receiver, Greg Dulcich at tight end. De'Von Achane is the offense. Willis's rushing ability is the only reason to consider him as a streamer.
8161.watch: Designed-run usage under Jeff Hafley's staff.

9758.outlook: Passing production has declined in each of his three seasons since a 24-touchdown rookie year that produced a ninth-place fantasy finish. Nico Collins is a legitimate No. 1 but the rest of the room is Kayshon Boutte, a hamstrung rookie in Jaylin Noel, and Tank Dell on IR. Stroud offers minimal rushing. He is a low-end QB2 in 1QB leagues and a matchup-dependent superflex starter.
9758.watch: Whether the offensive line and receiver depth improve his sack and pressure rate.

4943.outlook: Finished fifth in the NFL in passing yards for the second straight season and won a Super Bowl, and none of it produced fantasy value. The offense is run-first and Klint Kubiak, the coordinator who built it, left to be Las Vegas's head coach. Jaxon Smith-Njigba's Offensive Player of the Year season is the reason to consider Darnold at all in deep superflex formats.
4943.watch: How the new play-caller balances run and pass.

5870.outlook: Re-signed with Indianapolis and finished no lower than seventh in completion percentage and yards per attempt in his first season with the Colts. Anthony Richardson has been formally named the backup, which removes the week-to-week benching risk that dogged this job. Jones is a fine real-life starter and a marginal fantasy one, though his rushing keeps him streamable. Tyler Warren's production swings hard on Jones being healthy.
5870.watch: His own durability - Warren's value is tied to it.

9228.outlook: Three seasons in and he has not finished better than 20th in passing yards, 10th in rushing yards or 24th in points per game. Tetairoa McMillan is a real building block and Carolina's offense should be more competent, but nothing about the profile suggests fantasy relevance outside of two-quarterback desperation.
9228.watch: Whether McMillan's second-year leap drags him into streaming range.

12522.outlook: Eighth in the league in dropbacks and attempts as a rookie while managing only 5.9 yards per attempt, which is the whole story. Tennessee spent the fourth overall pick on Carnell Tate and signed Wan'Dale Robinson to fix the surrounding cast, and Robert Saleh's arrival should at least stabilize game scripts. His dynasty value fell 729 in 30 days on FantasyCalc, the sharpest drop among young quarterbacks in this file.
12522.watch: Whether Tate is ready to be a true No. 1 in Year 1.

3257.outlook: Positioned as Arizona's Week 1 starter and one of the biggest fantasy surprises of 2025, reeling off nine consecutive top-12 outings from Weeks 6 to 15. That stretch coincided with Trey McBride and Michael Wilson both producing at career-best rates. Mike LaFleur's arrival from the Rams should help, though the roster around him is thin and Carson Beck was drafted in the third round as the succession plan.
3257.watch: Whether Beck or Minshew gets a look if Arizona falls out of the race early.

13269.outlook: The No. 1 overall pick and reigning Heisman winner opens as the third quarterback behind Kirk Cousins and Aidan O'Connell, which is the single most important fact for his 2026 fantasy value. He is a big pocket passer with elite accuracy - a 7.1% career off-target rate, best in his class. FantasyPros dynasty has him QB17 while redraft sources have him around QB30, which is exactly the split you would expect for a rookie who is not starting.
13269.watch: When Las Vegas hands him the job.

1373.outlook: Traded to the Jets after an unsuccessful year in Las Vegas, and is in line to start. He peaked years ago and offers little rushing, so his fantasy relevance is minimal. His arrival matters far more for Garrett Wilson, who has had elite target volume and no quarterback play, than it does for Smith himself.
1373.watch: Whether Mike LaFleur's scheme raises the offense's efficiency.

96.outlook: Back for a second Steelers season at 42, reunited with Mike McCarthy, who ran top-five offenses in Dallas for three straight years. Pittsburgh finished in the bottom third on offense last season and Rodgers finished just outside fantasy relevance. The additions - Michael Pittman Jr., Rico Dowdle, Germie Bernard - are real but modest, and DK Metcalf and Pittman are both questionable for Week 1.
96.watch: Whether McCarthy's system meaningfully raises the pass volume.

6768.outlook: Named Atlanta's Week 1 starter, becoming the Falcons' sixth different opening-day quarterback in six years. His production and efficiency declined in Miami after a 4,624-yard, 29-touchdown 2023, and he has never been a rushing contributor. The weapons are better than anything he had recently - Bijan Robinson, Drake London, Kyle Pitts - and Kevin Stefanski's play-action scheme fits his skill set. Warm-weather NFC South games help.
6768.watch: Whether Stefanski's protection scheme keeps him upright and available.

11559.outlook: Out with a torn ACL, his third in five years, and listed as Atlanta's QB3 behind Tua Tagovailoa and Cooper Rush. He is not a 2026 fantasy asset in redraft. NBC's QB25 ranking is a notable outlier against a player who is currently unavailable, and it is the kind of stale ranking worth ignoring. His dynasty value actually rose 254 in 30 days, reflecting his contract and draft capital rather than any near-term role.
11559.watch: Whether the third ACL tear ends his run as a starting-caliber prospect.

12524.outlook: Backing up Deshaun Watson in Cleveland after a rookie year with eight appearances, 10 interceptions and a 57% completion rate. Todd Monken's arrival is the interesting variable, but Sanders is not a redraft asset unless Watson is benched or injured. Cleveland is openly building toward a top pick in the 2027 draft.
12524.watch: Whether Monken gives him the job at any point this season.

4017.outlook: The Week 1 starter in Cleveland largely because of his cap hit. He has appeared in 19 games since joining the Browns and averaged a poor 13.1 fantasy points across them, after being a top-six per-game quarterback in each of his first four NFL seasons. Cleveland traded Myles Garrett and is building for the future, so the leash is short.
4017.watch: How long before Shedeur Sanders or Dillon Gabriel gets the job.

1166.outlook: Opens as the Raiders' starter ahead of Fernando Mendoza after eight starts for Atlanta last season in which he averaged 12.5 fantasy points. He is 38 with no rushing value, and Klint Kubiak's system is built more around Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty than around the quarterback. This is a placeholder job with a defined expiration date.
1166.watch: How many weeks he holds off Mendoza.

11565.outlook: Lost the Minnesota job to Kyler Murray and is listed as QB3 behind Carson Wentz. He appeared in 10 games in 2025 with 11 touchdowns, 12 interceptions and a 58% completion rate after missing his entire rookie season. Only four sources ranked him, and his dynasty value dropped 483 in 30 days - the market is moving against him.
11565.watch: Whether Minnesota gives him another look if Murray gets hurt.

11604.outlook: Second among tight ends in fantasy points per game despite a late-game Week 1 injury that cost him five full games, and he still tied for fifth in the entire NFL with 13 end-zone targets. Bowers is the clear focal point of a Raiders passing game with a thin receiver room, whether Kirk Cousins or Fernando Mendoza is throwing. Klint Kubiak's arrival from Seattle is a scheme fit given how heavily his offenses lean on tight ends. Every source has him TE1 or TE2.
11604.watch: Whether the quarterback change mid-season disrupts his target share.

8130.outlook: Trails only Ja'Marr Chase in targets and receptions across the past two seasons among all pass catchers, not just tight ends, and led the position in every fantasy-relevant counting stat in 2025 with a position-high 15 top-12 weeks. He thrived specifically with Jacoby Brissett under center, and Brissett is the Week 1 starter again. FantasyPros, ESPN and Fantasy Football Calculator all rank him TE1 over Bowers. His redraft market value dropped 952 in 30 days, the largest fall of any tight end here.
8130.watch: Whether Mike LaFleur's scheme keeps him at a 25%-plus target share.

12517.outlook: Averaged 4.1 targets and 8.5 fantasy points across his first 14 NFL games, then leaped to 12.0 targets and 20.0 points per game over his final four including the playoffs - only 12 tight ends in NFL history have seen 10-plus targets in four straight games, and only one was a rookie. He was eighth or better among tight ends in yards per reception, per target and per route run. DJ Moore's trade to Buffalo opens up more volume. Unanimous TE3 across all eight sources.
12517.watch: Whether the four-game closing stretch was the new baseline or a small sample.

12518.outlook: Questionable with a groin injury entering Week 1. The split in his rookie year is stark: 13.1 fantasy points per game in 12 games with a healthy Daniel Jones, 6.3 and zero touchdowns in five without him. He was fifth among tight ends in end-zone targets and expected touchdowns, so the scoring should regress upward. Finished third among tight ends in targets and got three goal-line carries. Unanimous TE4 across seven sources.
12518.watch: Daniel Jones's availability, which historically swings Warren's production in half.

12506.outlook: Produced a 72-731-6 line plus 7-13-1 rushing as a 21-year-old rookie while sharing a room with David Njoku and cycling through quarterbacks, and his 108 targets rank eighth all time for a rookie tight end. Njoku left for the Chargers, which clears the room entirely. Touchdown regression is coming - seven scores against 3.8 expected on only three end-zone targets - but the volume is real. CBS is the low outlier at TE10 against a TE5 consensus.
12506.watch: Whether Todd Monken's arrival raises or caps his target share.

9484.outlook: Questionable in Week 1 coming off a Week 9 ACL tear and surgery, which is the entire evaluation. Before the injury he had back-to-back 10-target games and, through Week 8, only Jake Ferguson had more fantasy points at the position. The caveat is that six touchdowns came against 1.8 expected on two end-zone targets, so the scoring was unsustainable. Josh Jacobs's absence should push more of the offense through the air.
9484.watch: Whether he is on a snap count in September coming off the knee.

10859.outlook: Questionable with a hip issue. His 2025 was cut short by a back injury while he was on pace for a third straight top-10 finish (seventh in points per game). Since his 86-889-10 rookie year he has managed a combined 100-1,215-10 in 25 games, so the elite rookie production has not repeated. He remains third in the target pecking order behind Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams in one of the league's best offenses.
10859.watch: Whether the hip and back issues keep recurring.

7553.outlook: Finally delivered, finishing second among tight ends in routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy points with career highs in all but yardage, and made second-team All-Pro. The complication is that much of the production came with Kirk Cousins under center and Drake London sidelined, and Tua Tagovailoa is now the quarterback. Kevin Stefanski's scheme has historically been tight-end friendly. Sources are tight, TE6 to TE8 across the board.
7553.watch: Whether Tagovailoa's short-area accuracy sustains the target volume.

4217.outlook: Practiced in full uniform in Melbourne on Tuesday local time and is trending toward playing Thursday against the Rams, roughly eight months after tearing an Achilles in January's wild-card game. San Francisco cut a player to make room for a long snapper, which reporting framed as a signal Kittle is ready. He has finished sixth or better in points per game in most of his healthy seasons but has played one full year in his career and turns 33 this season. His market value actually rose 135 in 30 days.
4217.watch: Whether he is his usual self on the Achilles or a reduced-snap version.

10236.outlook: The position's biggest boom-or-bust profile. He led qualified tight ends in yards per target and per route run last year while playing only a 37% snap share, missing nine games over two seasons and never clearing six targets in a game. DJ Moore's arrival is a negative for his target share. His redraft value jumped 406 in 30 days, the largest positive move of any tight end in this file, which suggests the market expects a role increase.
10236.watch: Whether Buffalo finally plays him on more than 40% of snaps.

5022.outlook: The clearest touchdown-regression candidate at the position: 11 scores in 15 games after averaging 3.4 per year over his first seven seasons, against 5.1 expected touchdowns and only five end-zone targets. He has still finished 12th or better in points per game seven straight years, so the floor is real. A.J. Brown's departure frees up targets. He has missed at least two games in each of the past six seasons.
5022.watch: Touchdown regression against a possible target-share increase post-Brown.

1466.outlook: Re-signed for what may be his final season at 36. His 19.6% target share was the lowest since 2014 but he played all 17 games and still finished top 10 in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and points per game - a tenth straight top-five campaign. The scoring has dried up. FantasyPros dynasty is the outlier at TE22 for obvious age reasons while redraft sources cluster around TE10-TE12. Rashee Rice being healthy for a full season is a target-share negative.
1466.watch: Whether Mahomes coming off ACL surgery leans on him more or less.

8131.outlook: Signed with the Giants and reunited with John Harbaugh, finally getting a clean path to a full-time role after four years capped at 50% of Baltimore's snaps behind Mark Andrews. His one extended run with Andrews out - seven games, 23-356 receiving - is the best available sample. CBS is aggressive at TE8; the rest of the file has him TE9 to TE16. The Giants passing game depends heavily on Malik Nabers's knee.
8131.watch: Whether Harbaugh's offense actually gives him a 20% target share.

8110.outlook: Coming off a career year in which he ranked third among tight ends in receptions, touchdowns and end-zone targets with 10, producing nine top-12 weeks. The caveat that matters: his production dropped substantially in the games where both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens were healthy. Dallas throws enough for all three, but Ferguson is the one whose floor moves most with the receivers' availability.
8110.watch: Lamb and Pickens both staying healthy, which cuts his target share.

5012.outlook: Usage has fallen off a cliff over two seasons - 18th among tight ends in targets and outside the top 20 in catches and yards last year, after five straight top-five points-per-game finishes through 2023. A completely new coaching staff under Jesse Minter is either the reset he needs or confirmation the team has moved on. At 31 with Isaiah Likely gone, he has no internal competition, which is the bull case.
5012.watch: Whether the new staff restores him to a 20% target share.

7002.outlook: Career highs in targets, catches, yards and fantasy points, all eighth or better among tight ends, with nine top-12 weeks that tied for second at the position. He has been top 12 in average depth of target four straight years but has not been used near the goal line, with no more than four touchdowns or end-zone targets in each of the past three seasons. Jordyn Tyson opening on IR should push more targets his way early.
7002.watch: Red-zone usage - the volume is there, the scoring is not.

9480.outlook: Handled a solid 16% target share across the 12 games he was healthy as Jacksonville's clear No. 1 tight end, and it produced only 9.8 fantasy points per game. He has never cleared three touchdowns or four end-zone targets in a season, which is the recurring problem. The Jaguars receiver room got deeper, not thinner, so a target-share jump is unlikely.
9480.watch: Any change in his goal-line usage, which has never materialized.

3214.outlook: Reached 85 targets, 60 catches and 650 yards in each of the past two seasons, all top-10 marks at the position, and has been top 15 in average depth of target for seven straight years and top 12 in end-zone targets in seven of nine seasons. Despite that he has not finished top 12 in points per game since 2020. A.J. Brown's arrival is a clear negative for his target volume.
3214.watch: How many targets Brown takes out of his share.

5001.outlook: Ranked sixth or better among tight ends in targets, catches and yards but found the end zone only three times. That gap between volume and scoring has defined his career: one top-three season, in Dallas in 2021, and 10th or worse in every other campaign. With Tank Dell on IR and the receiver room thin behind Nico Collins, the target floor is safe.
5001.watch: Whether Houston finally uses him inside the 10.

8210.outlook: Signed with Washington after four years in Tennessee. He is one of only four tight ends to appear in all 68 games since entering the league and one of six with 50-plus catches in each of the past three years, so the availability is elite. The problem is he has never cleared a 16% target share and has eight career touchdowns on 11 end-zone targets. A healthy Jayden Daniels raises the floor.
8210.watch: Whether Washington uses him differently than Tennessee did.

12487.outlook: Questionable in Week 1 and listed as TE2 behind Colby Parkinson, which is the immediate obstacle. He was efficient in a small rookie sample behind Tyler Higbee, Parkinson and Davis Allen. FantasyPros dynasty ranks him TE15 while Fantasy Football Calculator has him TE32, one of the widest spreads at the position, and that gap is entirely about whether he wins the job.
12487.watch: Whether he passes Parkinson for the starting role.

13330.outlook: The No. 16 overall pick, questionable with an abdomen issue and listed behind Mason Taylor on the Jets depth chart. He broke out at Oregon with a 51-560-8 line on a 17% target share and aligned in the slot at a high rate. FantasyPros dynasty ranks him TE11 while CBS has him TE28 - the classic rookie split. His dynasty value fell 322 in 30 days, likely on the depth-chart news.
13330.watch: Whether he passes Mason Taylor for the primary tight end role.

5844.outlook: Has not been the same since a Week 16 ACL tear in 2023, following a 95-960-5 peak with 41-455-0 in 10 games in 2024 and a disappointing 2025. Kyler Murray's arrival is a scheme change worth noting - Murray historically leans on quick, middle-of-the-field targets. Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings are all ahead of or level with him in the pecking order.
5844.watch: Whether Murray's short-area game restores his target volume.

11603.outlook: Worked his way to the top of Seattle's depth chart and found the end zone seven times despite ranking 20th among tight ends in targets and yards. That is a touchdown-dependent profile in a run-first offense that just lost its coordinator. Jaxon Smith-Njigba commands a huge target share, and Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed are ahead of Barner for the leftovers.
11603.watch: Whether the new play-caller keeps him in the red-zone package.

8172.outlook: Back on the radar simply because he is atop Miami's depth chart. He flashed as a Denver rookie with a 33-411-2 line in 10 games and then essentially disappeared for two seasons. The Dolphins passing game is the weakest in the league after the teardown, with Malik Willis throwing to two rookies and Malik Washington. CBS is the aggressive outlier at TE18.
8172.watch: Whether the volume that comes with a bad offense translates to production.

12502.outlook: Caught 44 passes as a rookie playing behind Chig Okonkwo, which ranks 11th among rookie tight ends over the past decade. Okonkwo signed with Washington, so the job is his. Tennessee's offense is the limiting factor: Cam Ward averaged 5.9 yards per attempt as a rookie and the team added Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson ahead of Helm in the target order.
12502.watch: Whether Robert Saleh's offense can support a fantasy-relevant tight end.

7600.outlook: Has flirted with TE1 status twice, in 2022 and 2024, without ever holding it. Mike McCarthy's arrival is the reason for optimism - his Dallas offenses were consistently tight-end friendly - but Pittsburgh added Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard to a room that already had DK Metcalf. CBS is the low outlier at TE34.
7600.watch: Whether McCarthy's scheme features him the way it featured Jake Ferguson.

12493.outlook: A rookie season of extremes: 29.4 fantasy points in Week 7, 18.7 in Week 8, then one touchdown and 6.2 points per game the rest of the way. He is listed as the starter ahead of newly signed David Njoku, which is meaningful. NBC ranks him TE20 while Fantasy Football Calculator has him TE33. His dynasty value dropped 319 in 30 days.
12493.watch: Whether Njoku takes the job back.

8111.outlook: Ranks first among all tight ends in snaps since 2022 and second in routes, and it has produced almost no target volume. Mike Evans leaving frees up work, but Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin Jr. are ahead of him for it. Otton is a touchdown-dependent streamer in deeper leagues.
8111.watch: Whether any of Evans's 27 end-zone targets flow to him.

4066.outlook: An underwhelming first Denver season with a career-low 13% target share and 15th or lower among tight ends in routes, targets, catches and yardage. Jaylen Waddle's arrival makes the room more crowded, not less, alongside Courtland Sutton. At 32 in a Bo Nix offense that spreads the ball around, he is a bye-week option.
4066.watch: Whether Denver's target distribution changes at all with Waddle added.

2505.outlook: The listed starter in Carolina at 33 and the widest source disagreement at the position: CBS has him TE20 and ESPN TE28, while FantasyPros dynasty has him TE67. That 47-spot gap is entirely age versus current role. He is a touchdown-or-nothing play in an offense that has not supported a fantasy tight end.
2505.watch: His snap share once Carolina sees whether he can still separate.

4033.outlook: Signed with the Chargers after nine seasons in Cleveland and is listed as TE2 behind Oronde Gadsden II, which is the whole story for his 2026 value. He has been a productive fantasy starter in recent years but has not played a full season since 2018. Yahoo is the low outlier at TE43. He is a stash rather than a starter until the depth chart resolves.
4033.watch: Whether he overtakes Gadsden for the starting job.

12498.outlook: Played 81% of the Jets' offensive snaps and handled a 19% target share in 13 games as a rookie, which is excellent usage, and produced nothing because of the quarterback situation. Geno Smith is a real upgrade and Mike LaFleur's offense should be more efficient. First-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq is the direct threat to his snaps. ESPN and Yahoo have him outside TE40 while CBS has him TE27.
12498.watch: Whether Sadiq takes the job once healthy.

9482.outlook: Entering a contract year as the clear No. 2 behind Brock Bowers, a role that has never produced fantasy value. He has not come close to playing a full season. He is only relevant as a Bowers handcuff in tight-end-premium formats, which applies to both of Bobby's dynasty leagues.
9482.watch: A Bowers injury - that is the only path to relevance.

6865.outlook: Listed as the Rams' TE1 and graduated to a much larger role in the second half of last season, playing a substantial snap share from Week 10 on. Los Angeles runs a committee and second-year Terrance Ferguson is the more talented player. Matthew Stafford's volume makes even a moderate target share playable in deep leagues.
6865.watch: Whether Ferguson takes the job outright.

4993.outlook: Listed as Cincinnati's starter but has finished 23rd, 37th, 13th and 41st among tight ends over the past four seasons. Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown absorb nearly all of the meaningful target volume in this offense. A healthy Joe Burrow raises the whole offense, but Gesicki is a touchdown-dependent bye-week fill.
4993.watch: Whether Burrow's return produces enough volume to reach the TE3 role.

9221.outlook: Unanimous RB1 across all eight sources. Top 10 among backs in yards per carry, routes, targets, receptions, touchdowns and fantasy points in each of his three seasons, with 38 touchdowns over the last two - four more than anyone else. He has never finished a season higher than seventh in touches, and David Montgomery's trade to Houston removes the only thing capping that. The Lions offense returns intact.
9221.watch: Whether the touch share finally matches the talent with Montgomery gone.

9509.outlook: Unanimous RB2. Top five among backs in carries, rushing yards, touches, total yards and fantasy points in each of the past two seasons, plus no lower than fifth at the position in routes, targets, receptions and receiving yards in all three of his years. PFF charted him with 86 forced missed tackles, easily the most among backs. Kevin Stefanski's arrival is a positive for a workhorse profile.
9509.watch: Brian Robinson Jr.'s role as the change-of-pace back.

6813.outlook: Improved in points per game in each of the past three seasons and led the NFL in carries and touchdowns last year while finishing second in carries inside the 5 and fourth in fantasy points. The step forward came partly through the passing game, where he was top 10 among backs in routes. Daniel Jones returning as the starter keeps the offense stable.
6813.watch: Volume-driven wear at 27 after a league-leading carry season.

4034.outlook: Fully dressed for a second straight Melbourne practice and trending toward playing Thursday, though still listed questionable. He led all backs in snaps, routes, touches, targets, receptions, receiving yards, receiving touchdowns and fantasy points last season, on 450 touches including the playoffs. The concerns are real: 3.86 yards per carry, age 30, and the historical record on backs with that workload. FantasyPros dynasty is the outlier at RB12 while every redraft source has him RB3 to RB5. His redraft value rose 449 in 30 days.
4034.watch: The 450-touch workload catching up with him in the second half.

8138.outlook: Top five among backs in carries, rushing yards (league-high 1,621), touchdowns and yards per carry at 5.25, finishing sixth despite a minimal receiving role - his 40 targets ranked 26th at the position. Buffalo led the NFL in rushing and Joe Brady, who built that run game, is now the head coach. FTN is the outlier at RB9; everyone else has him RB4 to RB7.
8138.watch: Whether the receiving role ever expands - it is the only thing holding back his ceiling.

9226.outlook: Eleven or twelve touchdowns in each of his three seasons and a career-high 1,838 scrimmage yards. He has been top five among backs in targets and receiving yards in each of the past two years, which is the entire reason he holds this ranking in a gutted Miami offense. With Tua Tagovailoa and Jaylen Waddle gone and Malik Willis starting, Achane is essentially the only fantasy asset on the team, which should push his target share higher. Yahoo is the low outlier at RB11.
9226.watch: Whether Miami's low team totals cap his touchdown volume.

9224.outlook: The 2025 split tells the story: 10.1 fantasy points per game and one touchdown over his first seven games, then 21.2 points and 10 touchdowns over his final 10. The turnaround tracked Cincinnati's improved quarterback play, and a healthy Joe Burrow should sustain it. His redraft value rose 687 in 30 days, one of the sharpest positive moves among top-tier backs. Samaje Perine remains the only competition.
9224.watch: Burrow's health, which is what flipped his season last year.

4866.outlook: A real step back in 2025 - 1,413 yards and nine touchdowns on 317 touches after 2,283 and 15 on 378 in his first Eagles year - and he fell from first among backs in points per game to 15th. At 29 the age curve is a live concern, though Philadelphia's line and Jalen Hurts's presence near the goal line keep the touchdown equity high. Yahoo has him RB6, FantasyPros dynasty RB13.
4866.watch: Whether the touch volume stays north of 300 at age 29.

12507.outlook: Averaged 13.8 carries and 3.9 targets across nine appearances as a rookie, scored five touchdowns, averaged 15.1 fantasy points per game (13th best) and ranked third among backs in forced missed tackle rate per PFF. The competition is Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell, neither of whom threatens a three-down role. This is one of the cleaner bell-cow profiles in the file. FantasyPros dynasty and FTN both have him RB6.
12507.watch: Whether he holds up over a full 17-game workload.

8151.outlook: Signed with Kansas City as the reigning Super Bowl MVP and PFF's highest-graded back from 2025, moving into feature duties in an Andy Reid offense. His 2025 counting stats were career lows - five touchdowns, 11.3 points per game - because Seattle used a committee, but he still handled 252 touches. Emmett Johnson and Brashard Smith are the only competition. CBS is the high outlier at RB7.
8151.watch: Whether Mahomes's health keeps the offense scoring enough to feed him touchdowns.

12527.outlook: Questionable with a knee issue entering Week 1, and his redraft value has fallen 961 in 30 days - the sharpest drop of any top-15 back. As a rookie he was seventh among backs in carries, targets and receptions and eighth in forced missed tackle rate, and still could not overcome a bad Las Vegas offense. Klint Kubiak's arrival and a healthier line should help. FantasyPros dynasty has him RB3 and FTN RB5 against an RB11 consensus.
12527.watch: The knee, and whether Kubiak's system actually improves the run blocking.

3198.outlook: Second in the NFL in rushing yards for a fourth straight season at 32, with a league-leading 24 carries inside the 5. Since joining Baltimore he leads the NFL in carries inside the 5 with 42 and is second in touchdowns with 34. The entire coaching staff turned over under Jesse Minter, which is the only real question. Fantasy Football Calculator has him RB8, FantasyPros dynasty RB23 - the age split in one line.
3198.watch: Whether the new staff keeps giving him the goal-line work.

13287.outlook: Questionable with an ankle issue. The No. 3 overall pick led his rookie class in yards per carry (6.66) and yards after contact (4.16) and ranked second in forced missed tackle rate, with a genuine three-down skill set. Arizona's backfield is otherwise empty - James Conner and Trey Benson are both on IR - so the volume path is clear. His redraft value dropped 746 in 30 days, likely on the ankle. FantasyPros dynasty has him RB4.
13287.watch: The ankle, and whether Arizona's offense scores enough to support him.

8155.outlook: Franchise tagged, questionable with a thigh injury. He has finished 17th and 21st in points per game the past two years, a long way from top-eight finishes in his first two seasons, but he has produced 266-plus touches in each of the past three. Geno Smith and Mike LaFleur should raise the offense's efficiency meaningfully. Braelon Allen is the backup.
8155.watch: Whether LaFleur's offense finally gives him usable game scripts.

8150.outlook: Three straight seasons of 1,350-plus scrimmage yards, including a career-high 1,533, and one of only 11 backs in NFL history with 13-plus touchdowns in three of his first four seasons. His carry share fell last year but was offset by better efficiency and receiving work. Blake Corum is the established backup and has been effective. His redraft value rose 612 in 30 days.
8150.watch: Corum's carry share, which has crept up each season.

7588.outlook: Career bests across the board in his first Dallas year - 287 touches, 1,338 scrimmage yards, 4.77 yards per carry and 13 touchdowns after 16 across his first four seasons. He re-signed and has no meaningful competition, with Malik Davis and Emari Demercado behind him. Left guard Tyler Smith's thumb surgery is a short-term run-blocking concern. His redraft value rose 540 in 30 days.
7588.watch: Whether the efficiency holds without Tyler Smith on the left side.

7543.outlook: Signed with New Orleans after five years in Jacksonville, coming off a career-high 13 touchdowns and at least 1,399 scrimmage yards in three of the past four seasons. He has 35-plus catches in each of the last four years, which matters in full PPR. Kendre Miller and Audric Estime are the competition and Alvin Kamara has fallen to RB4. His redraft value rose 982 in 30 days, the largest gain of any back inside the top 20. NBC is the high outlier at RB12.
7543.watch: Whether Tyler Shough's offense generates enough red-zone trips.

11584.outlook: A bad 2025 - seven games missed, 3.40 yards per carry (fourth worst among qualified backs), 865 yards, four touchdowns, and zero carries inside the opponent's 5 - after a 5.42-yard, 1,514-yard rookie season. The talent case rests on the rookie year. Kenny Gainwell was signed as the complement, which is a real threat to third-down work. Sources are tight, RB17 to RB20.
11584.watch: Whether he gets goal-line carries at all this year.

6790.outlook: Questionable with an abdomen issue. Cleared 1,300 scrimmage yards in each of his first two Chicago seasons and scored 10 touchdowns last year, finishing 17th in points per game, but he ceded substantial work to Kyle Monangai down the stretch. The 2026 expectation is an even more even timeshare. Ben Johnson's offense is efficient enough that both backs can be usable in the right weeks.
6790.watch: How the Monangai split lands once both are healthy.

12481.outlook: Healthy and listed as the Giants' RB1 after a gruesome injury ended his rookie season - he has said publicly he considered retirement. Across his six full games he averaged 16.0 carries, 4.7 targets and 96.3 yards with six touchdowns, and his 19.1 points per game over that span would have ranked sixth for the full season. John Harbaugh's arrival should mean a heavy lead-back scheme. His redraft value fell 609 in 30 days despite no new injury news, which is worth noting.
12481.watch: Whether the leg holds up over a full workload.

12512.outlook: Handled a massive 71.4% share of Cleveland's designed rush attempts when healthy, 16.4 per game, though only at 3.6 yards per carry behind a poor line. The bookends of his rookie year were an off-field absence early and a season-ending leg injury in Week 16. Todd Monken's arrival and premium offensive draft capital should help the blocking. Dylan Sampson is the only competition.
12512.watch: Whether Cleveland's negative game scripts cut into his carry volume.

5892.outlook: Traded to Houston after a career-low year in Detroit - 182 touches, 908 yards, 9.8 points per game - though he was still efficient at 4.53 yards per carry and 2.28 after contact. He simply lost work to Jahmyr Gibbs. In Houston he is the clear lead back with Woody Marks behind him, and Montgomery has always been the goal-line option wherever he has played. The offense is the limiter.
5892.watch: Whether C.J. Stroud's offense produces enough red-zone trips.

12490.outlook: Takes over Jacksonville's lead role after Travis Etienne Jr. left, though he is questionable with an illness for Week 1. He played sparingly as a rookie - 83 carries, 14 targets - and cleared 10 touches only once, but scored in all four games where he had at least eight touches. That scoring rate will regress. Chris Rodriguez Jr. and LeQuint Allen Jr. are the competition for a committee that has not been settled.
12490.watch: Whether the job is actually his or a three-way rotation.

13286.outlook: The No. 32 overall pick lands in the cleanest opportunity of any rookie back: Kenneth Walker III signed with Kansas City and Zach Charbonnet opened on PUP with an ACL tear. Price posted a 4.13 yards-after-contact figure (second in his class) and a 3.6 forced missed tackle rate (third) at Notre Dame despite being stuck behind Jeremiyah Love. He caught 15 passes in 41 college games, so the receiving role is a real question. Seattle's offense is run-first.
13286.watch: Whether he handles passing downs or cedes them to George Holani.

12529.outlook: Three huge rookie games of 28-plus fantasy points and 8.3 points per game in the other 14, which is exactly what a committee back looks like. He was the more efficient of the two Patriots backs - 5.1 yards per carry, eighth best, an 83% catch rate and 10 touchdowns - but Rhamondre Stevenson held the lead role. He is questionable with a leg issue. His redraft value dropped 978 in 30 days, the second-sharpest fall of any back here. FantasyPros dynasty has him RB14, CBS RB31.
12529.watch: Whether he wins the New England lead job outright this season.

8228.outlook: Career highs in touches (251), yards (1,291) and touchdowns (eight), finishing 19th in points per game with 56 forced missed tackles per PFF, seventh at the position. Pittsburgh swapped Kenneth Gainwell for Rico Dowdle, which is an upgrade in competition, not a downgrade. Mike McCarthy's Dallas offenses were consistently productive for running backs.
8228.watch: How McCarthy splits the work with Dowdle.

7611.outlook: Held the New England lead role for most of last season, ranking fifth among backs in forced missed tackle rate, second in yards after contact (2.82) and first in yards per target (9.1). Those are not the numbers of a back about to lose his job. The Patriots offense was top-tier and A.J. Brown's addition should keep defenses honest. His redraft value rose 463 in 30 days while Henderson's fell.
7611.watch: Whether Henderson's efficiency eventually forces a role swap.

5967.outlook: Has handled 67.2% of the Titans' designed rush attempts over two seasons, 15.2 per game, and produced exactly five touchdowns in each - the offense is the problem, not the usage. His targets fell from 3.5 per game to 2.5 when Tyjae Spears was healthy. Robert Saleh's arrival and the additions of Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson should improve the scoring environment. Sources are tight, RB27 to RB30.
5967.watch: Whether Tennessee's offense generates enough red-zone trips to matter.

11583.outlook: Has appeared in one NFL game since being a 2024 second-round pick, having recovered from one ACL tear, returned in Week 12 of his rookie year, then retorn the same knee and missed all of 2025. He is questionable in Week 1 and listed as RB2 behind Chuba Hubbard, who is also questionable. At 23 with a genuine three-down skill set, the talent case is intact - the medical one is not.
11583.watch: Whether the knee holds up in live games.

7021.outlook: Two nearly identical seasons - 1,328 yards and five touchdowns on 274 touches in Dallas, 1,373 and seven on 275 in Carolina - at 4.57 yards per carry with 50 targets both years, finishing just inside the top 25 in points per game. He signed with Pittsburgh to share with Jaylen Warren under Mike McCarthy. That is a real committee, not a lead role.
7021.watch: Whether McCarthy gives him the early-down and goal-line work.

11581.outlook: Now the listed RB1 in Green Bay after Josh Jacobs was placed on the commissioner's exempt list on August 31 and became unavailable indefinitely. Lloyd has played one NFL game since being a 2024 third-rounder because of injuries, but he is healthy and was a full training-camp participant. His redraft value rose 1,249 in 30 days, the single largest positive move in the entire file. NBC and CBS have him RB26-27 while FantasyPros redraft and Fantasy Football Calculator still have him RB36 and RB40, which is the stale ranking to exploit.
11581.watch: Whether he can hold up as a lead back given his injury history.

7594.outlook: Questionable with a hamstring. Last season was a step back - 734 yards on 164 touches after clearing 275 touches and 1,100 yards in both 2023 and 2024 - and he lost lead duties to Rico Dowdle before Dowdle left. Dowdle's departure reopens the job, but Jonathon Brooks and AJ Dillon are both in the room. His redraft value fell 453 in 30 days.
7594.watch: The hamstring, and whether Brooks is healthy enough to take the job.

6806.outlook: Re-signed with Denver and must fend off RJ Harvey again. In the 10 games both were active last season, Dobbins took 153 carries (60% team share) to Harvey's 50, but Harvey out-targeted him 29 to 15. That split - Dobbins early downs, Harvey passing downs - caps both in full PPR. Rookie Jonah Coleman was added in the fourth round.
6806.watch: Whether Denver ever commits to a lead back.

12489.outlook: The passing-down half of Denver's committee, out-targeting J.K. Dobbins 29 to 15 across the 10 games both were active while taking only 50 carries to Dobbins's 153. In full PPR that receiving role is worth more than the raw carry gap suggests. FantasyPros has him RB31 against an RB35 consensus, which reflects the PPR skew.
12489.watch: Whether he takes over early-down work in Year 2.

11586.outlook: Two seasons as Kyren Williams's backup, averaging a healthy 5.1 yards per carry in the role, and 2026 projects the same. NBC is aggressive at RB28 while Fantasy Football Calculator has him RB41. He is one of the more valuable handcuffs in the file given how much volume Williams absorbs in a top offense.
11586.watch: Whether Los Angeles reduces Williams's workload to preserve him.

7567.outlook: Signed with Tampa Bay after a second-half breakout in Pittsburgh where he averaged 13.3 touches, 85.0 yards and 17.8 fantasy points. He steps into a Buccaneers backfield where Bucky Irving is coming off a 3.40-yard season, which makes this more of a genuine competition than a backup role. ESPN has him RB29 against an RB36 consensus.
7567.watch: How much passing-down work he takes from Irving.

12534.outlook: Questionable with a knee issue. Played 41% of Chicago's offensive snaps as a seventh-round rookie and forced his way into a committee with D'Andre Swift, which is remarkable draft-capital-adjusted usage. Ben Johnson's offense is productive enough to support two backs. FantasyPros dynasty has him RB31 against an RB37 consensus. His redraft value fell 308 in 30 days.
12534.watch: The knee, and whether the split moves further his way.

12533.outlook: Questionable and listed as Washington's RB1 ahead of Rachaad White, who is also questionable. He played 39% of Washington's snaps as a seventh-round rookie, which was heavily hyped but not fully realized. A healthy Jayden Daniels changes the offense's efficiency substantially. CBS has him RB32 while NBC has him RB43, one of the wider spreads in the RB30-45 range.
12533.watch: Whether the split with Rachaad White resolves in his favor.

5850.outlook: On the NFL commissioner's exempt list since August 31 while two misdemeanor charges are pending, which means he cannot practice or attend games and has no timetable to return. Green Bay's coach and general manager have said they hope he plays at some point this season. This is the clearest ranking-versus-availability contradiction in the entire file: the consensus still has him RB39 and FantasyPros dynasty has him RB27, while his redraft market value has collapsed 2,907 in 30 days - by far the largest drop anywhere in this data. Treat him as unrosterable in redraft until there is legal resolution.
5850.watch: Resolution of the pending charges - nothing else matters until then.

8136.outlook: Signed with Washington and is questionable for Week 1, sharing with Jacory Croskey-Merritt. He was a feature back in 2023, finishing top five among backs in touches, yards and fantasy points, and has been a committee piece since. His pass-catching keeps him relevant in full PPR even in a split. Sources are tightly clustered RB36 to RB44.
8136.watch: Whether he wins the passing-down role outright.

8408.outlook: Back for a second Minnesota season splitting with 31-year-old Aaron Jones Sr. His role last year was almost exactly as projected at 9.9 carries per game. Kyler Murray's arrival raises the offense's ceiling. CBS has him RB33 while FantasyPros dynasty has him RB44. His redraft value rose 367 in 30 days while Jones's fell 135, which suggests the market expects the split to tilt his way.
8408.watch: Whether he takes over the lead role from Jones outright.

4199.outlook: Listed as Minnesota's RB1 at 31 but coming off an injury-plagued year - 747 yards, his fewest since 2017, and three touchdowns in 12 games. He remained busy at 11.0 carries per game when active. The age curve and Jordan Mason's presence are both working against him, and his dynasty ranking of RB52 against an ESPN RB35 is the widest split on him.
4199.watch: Whether he can stay on the field for 17 games at 31.

10219.outlook: Signed with Jacksonville after three depth-role seasons in Washington, where he hit career highs of 115 touches, 530 yards and six touchdowns in 2025. He is listed as RB2 behind Bhayshul Tuten in a backfield with no established lead back. NBC has him RB39 against an RB44 consensus. His redraft value rose 188 in 30 days.
10219.watch: Whether Tuten's illness opens the door in September.

12474.outlook: Soaked up 220 touches as a rookie, 22nd among backs, but struggled badly with efficiency at 3.59 yards per carry and 1.61 after contact. Houston traded for David Montgomery specifically to take the early-down and goal-line work, so Marks projects into a passing-down and complementary role. Sources are unusually tight, RB42 to RB46.
12474.watch: Whether he keeps the receiving-down role with Montgomery added.

9753.outlook: On PUP with a torn ACL suffered in Seattle's playoff game against San Francisco, meaning he cannot play the first four games at minimum. He would otherwise have been the clear lead back with Kenneth Walker III gone. FantasyPros dynasty has him RB32 - a defensible dynasty price - while NBC has him RB54, and the gap is entirely about whether you are paying for this season or next. His redraft value fell 193 in 30 days.
9753.watch: Whether Jadarian Price locks down the job before he is cleared.

8132.outlook: Signed with Arizona and slots in behind Jeremiyah Love. He totaled 1,174 yards on 226 touches as an Atlanta rookie and has not approached that since playing behind Bijan Robinson. With James Conner and Trey Benson both on IR, Allgeier is the direct handcuff to a rookie carrying an ankle designation, which makes him one of the more valuable stashes here. His redraft value rose 343 in 30 days.
8132.watch: Love's ankle - Allgeier is the immediate beneficiary.

9508.outlook: A third season as Tony Pollard's change-of-pace back, a role that has never produced more than five touchdowns in a season. His presence measurably cuts Pollard's targets, from 3.5 per game to 2.5, which tells you where the receiving work goes. Tennessee's offense should be better under Robert Saleh but the ceiling here is a flex play in deep leagues.
9508.watch: Whether Pollard's workload drops enough to make him startable.

13345.outlook: A fourth-round rookie who lands in Denver's already-crowded J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey backfield, listed RB3. He is a 220-pound back who was highly efficient across four collegiate seasons at Arizona and Washington despite poor blocking. FantasyPros dynasty has him RB36 while Fantasy Football Calculator has him RB59 - the widest gap on any rookie back here.
13345.watch: Whether either Denver veteran gets hurt or traded.

13305.outlook: A fourth-round rookie behind Ashton Jeanty, and Jeanty is questionable with a knee issue. Washington ran a 4.33 forty at 6-foot-1 and 223 pounds, a 127 speed score. His redraft value rose 597 and dynasty 985 in 30 days, both among the largest gains in the file, which reflects the market pricing in Jeanty's injury. CBS has him RB40 against an RB49 consensus.
13305.watch: Jeanty's knee, which is the whole reason he is being drafted.

9511.outlook: Signed with the Chargers and will compete with Kimani Vidal for change-of-pace touches behind Omarion Hampton. He has been limited to a small career sample by injury. Yahoo has him RB43 against an RB50 consensus. He is a speed-based handcuff rather than a standalone play.
9511.watch: Whether he or Vidal wins the backup job outright.

12469.outlook: A second Cleveland season after a rookie year in which his 2.69 yards per carry ranked dead last among 65 qualified backs, though he contributed as a receiver. He is the direct backup to Quinshon Judkins, who has now had two seasons interrupted. Todd Monken's arrival and heavy offensive draft investment should improve the blocking. FantasyPros has him RB47, Yahoo RB57.
12469.watch: Judkins's availability - Sampson is the fallback in a high-volume backfield.

9225.outlook: Primary backup to Saquon Barkley in Philadelphia after working his way up following an in-season 2025 trade. He has been efficient on a small sample. Barkley at 29 coming off a 317-touch season with declining production makes this one of the better handcuff stashes in a strong offense. Yahoo has him RB48 against an RB53 consensus.

8154.outlook: Signed with Atlanta after a year as Christian McCaffrey's backup in San Francisco, and now works as the change-of-pace behind Bijan Robinson. He soaked up 200-plus touches in multiple Washington seasons, so the profile is a competent lead back stuck behind a star. He was not in last week's top 100 and enters at RB53 with seven sources covering him.
8154.watch: Bijan Robinson's workload, which has been near-total.

4035.outlook: Listed as RB4 on the New Orleans depth chart at 31 and carrying a knee designation, behind Travis Etienne Jr., Kendre Miller and Audric Estime. Only two backs age 31 or older have posted a top-30 fantasy season over the past seven years. Fantasy Football Calculator has him RB46 and NBC RB62 - the disagreement is about whether he has any role at all. His redraft value has fallen to 111, essentially nothing.
4035.watch: Whether he holds a roster spot, let alone touches.

11576.outlook: A slow start in 2025 was followed by a season-ending knee injury in Week 4. Through the first three weeks he played 28% of the Jets' snaps for 67 yards and a touchdown on 16 touches. He is the direct backup to Breece Hall, who is questionable with a thigh injury and playing on the franchise tag. Sources are tightly clustered RB52 to RB58.
11576.watch: Hall's thigh - Allen is the immediate handcuff.

13337.outlook: A fifth-round Chiefs rookie whose 3.4 career forced missed tackle rate was fourth best in his class, producing 1,451 rushing yards. He is competing with Brashard Smith for the No. 2 role behind Kenneth Walker III. His dynasty value rose 767 in 30 days. ESPN is the low outlier at RB69 while NBC and CBS have him RB50.
